metadata.note: Rail routes into Ocean City, NJ, and the PRR beach lines of Cape May County, built from research/branches/ocean_city_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-20), drawing only its drawable: spans. Two unrelated companies were called 'Ocean City Railroad' - the 1884 West Jersey construction subsidiary (Sea Isle City - Ocean City, consolidated into the West Jersey 1 Sep 1885) and the c.1896 Reading-side company (Petersburg - Ocean City, merged into the Atlantic City RR 14 Jun 1901). Neither is known to have run trains in its own name, so no feature carries that company. Rule 4 splits: West Jersey / West Jersey and Atlantic -> West Jersey and Seashore at the 4 May 1896 consolidation (identical geometry); Atlantic City RR -> Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines 15 Jul 1933 (the ACRR years stay in atlantic_city_railroad.geojson, acrr-ocean-city-branch); PRSL -> Conrail 1 Apr 1976. The Atlantic City and Shore (Shore Fast Line) is its own company despite PRR stock control - it ran its own cars. The Shore Fast Line is two features because its two sections have different drawn end years (1946 / 1947).
metadata.color_note: New colours chosen 2026-10-20 and checked against every colour in data/: West Jersey Railroad #BF2687, West Jersey and Seashore Railroad #A5BF26, West Jersey and Atlantic Railroad #723333, Atlantic City and Shore Railroad #26BABF. Pulled programmatically: Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines #2A6F97 from pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson (note: the same hex is the Reading's, flagged in atlantic_city_railroad.geojson's color_note); Conrail #3E6FD0 from metro_north.geojson. The West Jersey and Atlantic is treated as its own company (a separate PRR-controlled corporation, Newfield - Atlantic City, named as the operator in the research report). If a source shows its trains were worked by the West Jersey Railroad, recolour wja-somers-point-branch to the West Jersey colour.
not_drawn: West Jersey and Seashore / PRSL on the beach lines after 15 Jul 1933 (sjrail '1934'): single ambiguous source; no PRSL passenger year confirmed.

West Jersey and Atlantic Somers Point Branch 1882-1892 and WJ&S steam 1898-1906: unconfirmed by any timetable.
Pleasantville & Ocean City / Philadelphia & Atlantic City, Pleasantville - Somers Point 1880-1882: already drawn as pac-pleasantville-somers-point in atlantic_city_railroad.geojson (untouched).
Sea Isle City Motor Line (steam dummy, Railroad Ave, 1897t): drawable NONE - not established as a separate service.
South Jersey Railroad, Tuckahoe - Sea Isle City 1893 [ANCHOR]: single-year anchor block, not drawn per instructions; route (via Petersburg or via Sea Isle Junction) also unresolved.
Ocean City RR / South Jersey RR, Ocean City Junction - Ocean City 1897 [ANCHOR]: operator not established; not drawn.
Atlantic City RR Ocean City Branch 1901-1933: already drawn as acrr-ocean-city-branch in atlantic_city_railroad.geojson (checked, agrees with the report).
Atlantic City RR / PRSL Sea Isle City Branch (Ocean City Jct - Sea Isle City): drawable NONE - no confirmed passenger year.
PRSL Ocean City 10th St - 4th St / Ocean City Gardens: no confirmed PRSL passenger year; track abandoned 11 Sep 1958.
'Ocean City Electric Railway' (in-town trolley): no evidence it existed.
Ocean City Branch Oct 1981 - Oct 1982: no passenger trains after 15 Oct 1981 (Rule 1).
not_yet_sourced: West Jersey beach line Sea Isle City - Ocean City START [OPEN]: 1889 is the first confirmed year (Fowler 1889t). Wikipedia/ocnjmagazine say Dec 1884, westjersey.org says 1890 - unresolved; Bridgeton Pioneer Dec 1884 / 1885 pages (Chronicling America) are the obvious next check.
West Jersey Stone Harbor Branch START [OPEN] 1893 (first confirmed, Fowler z) and WJ&S END [OPEN] 1897 (last confirmed, Fowler 1897t); real dates unknown.
West Jersey and Atlantic Somers Point Branch START [OPEN] 1893 (first confirmed) and WJ&S END [OPEN] 1897 (last confirmed).
Shore Fast Line Atlantic City - Somers Point END [OPEN] 1947: closure 18 Jan 1948 vs Feb 1948, both second-hand.
Shore Fast Line Somers Point - Ocean City END: 1946 (storm/fire, second-hand) vs 1948 (Wikipedia) - drawn to 1946.
PRR beach lines END: 1933 (Wikipedia; fall-1933 bridge rebuild) vs 1934 (sjrail).

PRR lease of the West Jersey and Seashore from 1 Jul 1930: whether the PRR rather than the WJ&S ran the trains 1930-33 (a possible Rule 4 split for the Sea Isle City and Ocean City features) should be decided once for the whole WJ&S system.
Sea Isle City station site, the island right of way through Ludlam Island, Strathmere, Avalon and Stone Harbor, and the Great Egg Harbor Bay trestle are not located; drawn as labelled straight legs.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

segments.note: West Jersey and Seashore (PRR system) from the 4 May 1896 consolidation. Confirmed by an 1897 company timetable (Fowler '1897t'). The PRR leased the WJ&S from 1 July 1930; whether the PRR rather than the WJ&S ran the trains 1930-33 (which would need a Rule 4 split) is unresolved. By Feb 1952 Sea Isle City was reached only by bus. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

segments.note: West Jersey Railroad beach line from Sea Isle City up Ludlam Island and Strathmere, over Corson's Inlet and through Ocean City at street level to a pier at 2nd Street (Whale Beach, Corson's Inlet, Middle Thoroughfare, Peck's Beach / 55th St, 34th St, 14th St, 8th St). Built by the Ocean City Railroad (1884), a West Jersey construction subsidiary consolidated into the West Jersey 1 Sep 1885; no evidence it ran trains in its own name, so it is not a separate company here. OPENING CONFLICT: Wikipedia says the 11.25-mile extension opened December 1884 and ocnjmagazine dates the West Jersey's Corson's Inlet bridge to 1884; westjersey.org's year maps put the line under 1890; the earliest timetable found is 1889 (Fowler: 'Ocean City 1889t', 'Central Avenue 1889t', 'Middle Thoroughfare 1889t'). 1889 is drawn as the FIRST CONFIRMED year, NOT the opening - service very probably began 1884/1885, but no timetable or newspaper before 1889 has been found. Do not move the start earlier without such evidence. Ends 1896 at the 4 May 1896 West Jersey and Seashore consolidation. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

Drawn on the standard-gauge grade as rebuilt from June 1882 (the era drawn here). The existing feature pac-pleasantville-somers-point (atlantic_city_railroad.geojson, 1880-1882) uses the same bike path but stops short at both ends (5.0 mi, ending about 1.3 mi north of the path's Somers Point end), so it was not reused; that feature was not changed. segments.note: West Jersey and Atlantic Railroad (PRR system) branch, Pleasantville - Smith's Landing - Northfield - Linwood - Sea View - Maltby - Somers Point, with a steamboat on to Ocean City (the boat is not drawn). The WJ&A leased the Pleasantville & Ocean City RR on 1 June 1882 and regauged it from 4 June 1882 (Wikipedia, via atlantic_city_railroad.txt); 1882-1892 is probable but rests on corporate continuity, not a timetable. 1893 is the FIRST CONFIRMED year (Fowler 'z' = 1893 Official Guide at every station), not the start of WJ&A service; do not move it earlier without a timetable. A March 1895 joint timetable runs Somers Point trains out of Atlantic City via Pleasantville. Ends 1896 at the 4 May 1896 consolidation into the West Jersey and Seashore. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

Documented: Wikipedia 'about 11 miles' for the ACS's own line; a second-hand summary gives 'roughly 18 mile' for the whole Atlantic City - Ocean City run (this feature plus acs-somers-point-ocean-city draws 15.74 mi). Real-traced: in Atlantic City on the PRR-tagged Atlantic Avenue (street trackage) from Virginia Avenue and on the PRR-tagged Bacharach Boulevard approach (0.56 mi); about 1.2 mi on the present NJ Transit Atlantic City Line track (untagged) between the Atlantic City terminal area and the Newfield Branch grade - a LATER alignment may be drawn there, the 1907 WJ&S approach is not separately mapped; then the PRR-tagged Newfield Branch grade (the West Jersey and Seashore's electrified Newfield - Atlantic City line, over which the ACS cars ran) to Pleasantville; then the Pleasantville to Somers Point Bike Path (old_railway_operator='PRSL (PRR)'). Approximated with straight lines: Atlantic Ave (Ohio Ave) - Bacharach Blvd gap 0.46 mi; connector, present Atlantic City Line - Newfield Branch grade 0.11 mi; connector, Newfield Branch fragments 0.04 mi; connector at Pleasantville junction 0.16 mi (total 0.77 mi). The Virginia Avenue terminal is placed where Virginia Avenue crosses the tagged Atlantic Avenue track; whether cars ran on to the Boardwalk is not established.

segments.note: Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (the Shore Fast Line), electric interurban: Atlantic City (Virginia Ave) over the West Jersey and Seashore's electrified line to Pleasantville, then its own line over the former Somers Point Branch via Northfield and Linwood to Somers Point (Country Club). PRR/WJ&S stock control is NOT a Rule 4 split - the ACS ran its own cars. Starts 1907, the first dated year (ocnjmagazine: first car into Ocean City 1 July 1907; Wikipedia 'ran from 1907'); a 1906 start on this section is unverified and not drawn. From 1931/32 cars ran from the WJ&S Tennessee Ave station during repairs to a fire-damaged trestle (Fowler line 120). END: the line was replaced by buses in January/February 1948 (one summary gives 18 January 1948, another February 1948; Wikipedia 'until 1948'). Drawn to 1947, the LAST CONFIRMED full year - service ran into January 1948, but the closing date is second-hand. Do not extend to 1948 without a primary source. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: ocnjmagazine.com/?p=11254 (1 Jul 1907); Wikipedia "Atlantic City and Shore Railroad" (1907-1948); branchline.uk Fowler line 120 (stops, 1931/32 Tennessee Ave). 1947/1948 end second-hand (search-engine summaries only). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (Shore Fast Line) Ocean City leg: Somers Point over the Great Egg Harbor Bay trestle to Ocean City at 8th Street, Bay Street, the PRR station and the Boardwalk at 8th Street. Opened 1 July 1907 (ocnjmagazine). END CONFLICT: a railfan source (search summary only) says the Ocean City leg was 'cut in 1946 because of storm damage to the Somers Point causeway' and another that the bay bridge 'burned in 1946'; Wikipedia says the whole line ran 'until 1948, when a hurricane damaged the viaduct'. segments.note: Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines, formed 15 July 1933 when the Atlantic City Railroad (Reading) leased the West Jersey and Seashore. The ex-Reading line Tuckahoe - Petersburg - Palermo - Crook Horn - Ocean City became the only rail route to Ocean City once the ex-PRR beach line closed (1933/34). Through PRR New York - Ocean City trains ran over it: the Feb 1952 Official Guide shows arrivals at 'Ocean City (10th St.)' with legible times, confirming service in 1951-52. The ACRR -> PRSL change is a real Rule 4 split even though the ACRR corporation became the PRSL. Ends 1976: Conrail took over PRSL operations on 1 April 1976. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

segments.note: Conrail operated the remaining PRSL passenger service from 1 April 1976 under New Jersey DOT subsidy (NJ Transit did not take over Conrail's commuter operations until 1983, after this line had closed). Last train 15 October 1981, ending service when a ring gear failed on the Crook Horn drawbridge (sjrail); 34th Street station last served 13 August 1981 (Wikipedia). Abandonment notices were posted at the 51st, 24th and 10th St stations in October 1982 - an abandonment year, not a passenger year, so 1982 is not drawn. The Crook Horn bridge was removed November 1992. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
